description: Jatoba is a very hard, heavy tropical hardwood whose salmon to reddish-brown heartwood darkens markedly with light exposure. It is widely sold as 'Brazilian cherry' flooring and is also used for furniture, stair parts, and tool handles.

hazards.summary: Occupational asthma has been reported in a woodworker exposed to jatoba dust, in a report that also covered tali wood. Details of how the diagnosis was confirmed could not be checked.
All wood dust, including jatoba, is classified by IARC as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nose and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: The same report implicated tali (Erythrophleum spp.), an unrelated African legume timber.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed jatoba (Hymenaea courbaril) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Salmon-orange to reddish-brown heartwood with darker reddish-brown streaks, beside a strip of greyish-white sapwood. Interlocked grain with a medium to coarse texture, visible open pores scattered across the face, and a warm golden luster. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.

notes_internal: Quirce-2004 confirmed (PMID 14767459, DOI 10.1016/j.jaci.2003.11.018) but is a letter with no abstract; full text blocked (403). If it reports a positive specific inhalation challenge (likely for this group, but unconfirmed), upgrade to level 1. Number of patients and which wood each reacted to also unconfirmed. Not in WIS30 or SENSOR-2017 tables. Name checked on GBIF only. No reports for a given effect does not mean the wood is safe.
